name: Chroma Denoise
description: Remove blotchy or swimming colour noise
longDescription:
CCD — Camcorder Colour Denoise — cleans up noisy colour while leaving detail in the picture alone. It averages each pixel's colour with nearby pixels whose colour is close enough to be the same thing, so flat areas smooth out and edges stay put.

Use it when the picture is watchable but the colour is a mess: the crawling red and blue blotches on VHS captures, and the chroma noise old camcorders produce in low light. Because it never touches luma, it can be pushed much harder than a general denoiser before the picture looks soft.

Run it after deinterlacing. Raising Temporal Radius above 0 pulls in neighbouring frames, which cleans up more but can smear fast colour movement.

methods.name: CCD
methods.description: Camcorder Colour Denoise — spatial, for blotches that stay put

methods.name: Cnr4
methods.description: Temporal, gated on movement — for colour that swims or shimmers frame to frame rather than sitting still

ui.label: Method
ui.description: CCD smooths blotchy colour in place. Cnr4 settles colour that shifts between frames.

ui.label: Threshold
ui.description: How different a neighbouring pixel's colour may be and still be averaged in. Higher cleans more and can bleed colour across edges

ui.label: Temporal Radius
ui.description: Frames on each side to average with. 0 works on each frame alone; higher cleans more but can smear fast colour movement

ui.label: Near Samples
ui.description: Include the closest ring of sample points

ui.label: Mid Samples
ui.description: Include the mid-distance ring of sample points

ui.label: Far Samples
ui.description: Include the outermost ring of sample points. Cleans large blotches at the cost of speed and some colour bleed

ui.label: Sample Scale
ui.description: How far apart the sample points sit. Left off, this is derived from the frame height (CCD was written for 240p), which is almost always what you want

ui.label: Strength
ui.description: How far colour is pulled toward the surrounding frames. The default already sits near the top of the range, so there is far more room downward than up.

ui.label: Motion sensitivity
ui.description: How much movement is tolerated before the filter stops correcting. Raise it if noise survives in moving areas; lower it if moving colour smears.

ui.label: Temporal radius
ui.description: How many frames either side are considered. Higher is stronger and slower.

ui.label: Detail retention
ui.description: Higher settings protect fine chroma detail at the cost of some smoothing.

ui.label: Weighting
ui.description: How neighbouring frames are weighted against the current one.
